newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia April palm oil output seen up eight pct.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia April palm oil output seen up eight pct.

text.p: Malaysian palm oil output in April was estimated to have risen by up to eight percent over March, plantation houses said on Tuesday.
The Palm Oil Registration and Licensing Authority (PORLA), which is scheduled to release official crop data for April on May 15, put March production at 683,196 tonnes.
"There was a rise in April output but it was smaller than the previous month which posted a 36 percent rise," an official at a plantation firm said.
Another plantation official said April's rise was due to large harvesting from replanted areas in the eastern Malaysian state of Sabah. "Also, this is the high harvest season," he said.
Palm oil output normally peaks at around October/November.
Private crop forecaster Ivan Wong had earlier projected a rise of six percent in April output to 723,000 tonnes.
Traders estimated end-April stocks at 695,000-705,000 tonnes against 689,633 tonnes at end-March.
Exports in April were estimated at 600,000-610,000 tonnes against PORLA's figure of 565,219 tonnes in March.
